content:
I tried to get fluent enough in lean that I could do something useful a year ago. Life did life things, so now we're trying again.

I'm trying to formalize some fairly easy finite group theory results because the math is straightforward but it's everything I struggle with in the api.

For these two results I need a bunch of basic group theory facts which I'm sure are there but Loogle is decisively winning right now. For the first sorry for instance we need the second isomorphism theorem to argue that since (M \sup N) / N is isomorphic to M / (M \cap N), and both groups on the RHS are p-Groups then the left is a p-Group, and from N being a p-Group M \sup N is a p-Group. I can't even find the second isomorphism theorem in Loogle, just a version for additive subgroups? And how do we find our results that if (M \sup N) / N is a p-Group and N is a p-Group then M \sup N is a p-Group?

Rather than a bunch of citations for results, how do you do your search process to get basic stuff like this? I think one of the biggest struggles when moving beyond the sandbox is needing to learn how to find results since nothing has a name I can guess.

Similarly for the second sorry, there has to be results about the comap (that's what we call the pre-image right?) of a sSup which would make this quick and easy but my struggles are in finding the results. Are you just searching for theorem names with the string literal "sSup"? That didn't produce much.

import Mathlib
variable {G : Type*} [Group G] (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)]
open Subgroup

theorem IsPGroup.sup {M N : Subgroup G}
    (hM_normal : M.Normal) (hN_normal : N.Normal)
    (hM_p : IsPGroup p ↥M) (hN_p : IsPGroup p ↥N) :
    IsPGroup p ↥(M ⊔ N) := by
  sorry

/-- The Fitting subgroup of a group is the supremum of the normal nilpotent subgroups -/
def fitting (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  sSup { N : Subgroup G | N.Normal ∧ Group.IsNilpotent N }

/-- The Fitting subgroup is characteristic. -/
instance fitting_characteristic : (fitting G).Characteristic := by
  rw [characteristic_iff_comap_eq]
  intro φ
  dsimp [fitting]
  sorry
:search: IsPGroup.to_sup_of_normal_left, IsPGroup.to_sup_of_normal_right, and 2 more
looks like that one doesn't exist, let's try instead @loogle Subgroup.comap, OrderIso
:search: MulEquiv.coe_comapSubgroup, AddSubgroup.toSubgroup_comap, and 1 more
:search: OrderIso.map_sSup_eq_sSup_symm_preimage, OrderIso.map_sSup, and 5 more

In case you're doing this for Mathlib, note that the first theorem exists (docs#IsPGroup.to_sup_of_normal_left) and the Fitting stuff is being worked on (#39813). I kinda assumed Kim Morrison would define the subgroup after the theorem is merged.

So for exploring our options with loogle I see an example of searching for the type of thing we want to prove using wildcards with the first example. For the second example we're specifying a place in the name space, that we want a general statement which shows equality between two things, and a substring? This seems like there is an art to using search well.

That's cool they're checking that in, I'll focus on some lemmas for interesting properties of the fitting subgroup and not fitting's theorem. I was going to do the p-core argument instead of commutators, which only works for finite groups so their version is more general.
p-core is in #39771 if you need it
@Ryan Smith Are you aware of https://leansearch.net (might be down right now) or https://leanexplore.com? They can help you find things using natural language queries

A bunch of the simple stuff I thought needed doing is already somewhere deep in the PR queue. Which is great, though it does mean we have a few less low hanging fruit to work on newbie skills.

Are these changes being actively reviewed or are they stuck in limbo?
Are these being actively maintained? I remember getting burned on moogle which seemed ok but stopped updating, so I ended up confused when stuff which I was positive must be there didn't show up :)

What areas are you interested in?

There are also a bunch of presentation stuff being worked on, see #Geographic locality > Madrid, Spain and #ItaLean 2025 > Projects: Finitely Presented Groups for updates if you're interested.

I'm not sure but I think character theory could use some love if you're interested, e.g. working towards Burnside's p q.

Funny you should mention Burnside’s theorem. That was actually what I wanted to do a year ago but I finally ran out of steam trying to figure out how express a sum over the irreducible characters of a finite group. Some people suggested using a skeleton category but then we’ve left FDRep and all of the results there. There were other places where it was hard to formalize involving the characteristic polynomial but the irreducible characters was the hardest road block.

I was looking into doing the pure group theory version of the proof, which has a lot more steps but starts with the Fitting subgroup.
